note: Merged from batch files; interrupted batches were finished by further independent agents with the same instructions (part names record which).

scores.notes: Empty wheeled throne made entirely of flame in the centre, framed by cloud, with no face, hands or figure in the seat; Daniel in linen tunic and indigo fringed cloak stands small at the lower centre. Gold ground and a dark green ground band reach all four borders; city placed along the top rather than below, only one throne shown.

Watercolor: Jesus stands centre before the rolled-aside stone with his arm extended toward the tomb. Martha has her hands on her chest beside him, the shrouded Lazarus stands in the dark tomb mouth, and the crowd and olive trees fill the scene. Paint reaches all four borders and no lettering is visible.

Courtyard with haloed elder on a stool pointing at a scroll, boy in the doorway, lamp and jar on the ledge all match; but the unrolled scroll in the lower-centre foreground carries about seven lines of glyph-like pseudo-script. The scroll lies on the ground rather than on his knees; all four edges are painted through.

Bottom-left and bottom-right corners show unpainted cream paper where the wash stops short of the border. Peter (left foreground) steps off a wooden pier/platform rather than from the boat, which sits apart at right with disciples rowing, while Jesus stands on the water center under a cloud break.

Exiles seated on the reedy bank in the foreground, several with hands over faces, across the water a walled Babylon with ziggurat at upper right and small lamps on the towers. Painting runs to all four edges; the gate's tiled panels are pattern, not lettering; sky is gold rather than dusk-dark.

Four soldiers crouch, casting pebble lots over folded garments, with the crucified Jesus at right. His titulus carries squiggled glyph lines (upper right). A white-paper border with a ragged wash edge runs around all four sides.

Four winged creatures with eyes on their wings (lion, calf, man, eagle) flank an empty throne that holds only a starburst of light under a rainbow, with no face or figure in it; the glassy floor and clouds form the sea of glass. The watercolour linework and washes reach all four borders; there is no lettering in the corners.

Rows of glyph-like pseudo-script fill the open scroll on the elder's knees (center); the scene asks for a scroll of names, so the writing is requested but still visible lettering. Otherwise matches: elder on stool pointing, youth in the doorway at right, lamp and jar on the ledge; warm wash reaches all four borders.

Job sits on a grey ash heap with broken pots at lower centre, holding a staff and gazing up at a dust whirlwind upper centre-right; its fiery core is swirling light only, with no face or figure on close inspection. Walled village at left, painting reaches all borders, no lettering.

Dark interior: the Levite stands with the knife held low over the still concubine on a mat. A clay lamp sits on a bench, and the donkey with a cloak is in the doorway. There is no gore, the painting is dark to every edge, and the small plaque on the wall carries no letters.

The roles are reversed: haloed Jesus stands inside the boat (centre) while Peter, carrying a net and staff, walks on the waves toward it (left), so Peter is not stepping out to come to Jesus on the water. On zoom, faint scratched glyph-like marks appear on the lower hull just right of centre (~x930-970, y625).

Watercolor wash breaks irregularly into cream unpainted paper along the bottom border and at the bottom-left/right corners and side edges. Content matches: fire streaks fall from a dark cloud onto two walled cities, smoke, palms, fleeing figures on the road, sunrise; no face in the cloud.

Ezekiel stands at right with right arm raised over a valley strewn with skulls and bones, but faces the viewer and holds a clipboard-like wooden board with a clip and a pen at chest height (blank, no writing), an odd anachronistic prop. Gold sky and ground reach all four edges; no figure for God.

Ezekiel stands with his arm raised over skulls and ribcages in a wide barren valley in amber light. The cloudy sky (top) holds no face or figure, so God is absent. Edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

Saul stands centred in a shaft of white light looking up, companions at right shield their eyes, and a walled city sits on the left horizon; the light holds no figure. The sky is stormy rather than clear, a minor deviation; the edges are fully painted and the corners have no lettering.

Shulammite in red mantle center-left gestures toward lilies and roses, faint incised halo ring behind her head, shepherd's crook in the grass at right, vineyards and stone village behind. Gold-leaf sky and meadow reach all borders with no frame or lettering.

The concubine on the mat in the lower foreground has wide-open eyes looking at the viewer, head on a pillow and hand on her chest, so she reads as a living woman resting while the Levite stands over her with a knife, contradicting the 'still form' after her death. The Levite (centre) also has a faint halo ring behind his head; lamp, bench, cloak and donkey in the doorway are present, edges full.

In this icon style, an elder on a stool points at a scroll covered in rows of pseudo-Latin lettering (centre). A boy in blue listens by the doorway, and a lamp and jug sit on the ledge. The scene asked for a line of names, but the visible lettering is a text defect. Edges are full.

Job, covered in sores, sits upright on a grey ash heap among potsherds (left-centre) and looks up toward a dust whirlwind with fiery light in its core (centre-right); the vortex holds no face or figure. The watercolour washes reach all four borders, with only paper-light highlights near the horizon and bottom-left, and the corners have no lettering.

Gold-leaf spandrels fill the top-left and top-right corners outside an arched dark interior, making an arched icon-panel frame. Jonah sits hunched with cloak drawn inside the ribbed fish interior; the faint golden glow panels in the walls contain no face or figure.

The unrolled scroll on the wall in the lower centre-right is covered in dense lines of glyph-like pseudo-script (requested by the scene, but visible writing). The watercolour washes fade into unpainted white paper at the lower-left corner and along the bottom-right; villagers, woman with jar, two Roman soldiers and child in doorway all present.

The soldiers kneel casting lots under a close crucifix. Behind them stand about ten unrequested onlookers, several styled as Jesus doubles: long-haired, bearded men in blue mantles over white tunics (centre-left, centre and right, one leaning on a shield). This duplicates the crucified figure.

The elder on a rush stool has the scroll open on his knees and points at it, the boy stands in the doorway (right), and the lamp and jugs sit on a ledge (lower right), all as requested; but the open scroll (centre) shows about eight lines of glyph-like pseudo-script. All four edges are painted through.

A scrawled painted signature appears on the waves in the bottom-right corner. Otherwise matches: Peter (center-left, holding a staff and net) steps from the boat onto the waves toward Jesus standing on the water at right under moonlight, disciples in the boat.

Child in a plain tunic stands centre with an open hand, wolf lying with two lambs at left, leopard with young goat and calves and a young lion at right, lioness at far left, villagers watching at right and walled Jerusalem with temple at upper left. Oil painting reaches all four edges; no signature in any corner.

An elder on a wooden stool points at a scroll on his knees filled with dense pseudo-Hebrew script (centre). A boy stands in the doorway, with a lamp and jug on the ledge at right. The lettering is clearly legible as script. Edges are fully painted.

The content matches: old Adam lies on a woven mat with hands on his chest, kin kneel around him, with tents, mud-brick houses, a well, goats, a jar and tools. But the watercolour vignettes into white paper with splatter dots along the left, bottom and right borders and in all four corners.

Sky washes stop short of the left border at upper left, leaving white unpainted paper along the left edge down to the horizon. David reclines in grass beside a still pool with sheep, crook and stone fold (plus an unrequested harp and sword); he is large mid-right rather than small.

Moses with a staff leads a long column of families, children on shoulders and bundles, along the seabed between towering water walls at left and right under a dark stormy sky. The requested pillar of cloud and fire is absent (no form for God at all) and an unrequested walled town sits on the far shore at upper right; ink-and-wash reaches all four edges.

Icon on a gold sky: Paul in a dark mantle with a scroll tucked in his belt gazes upward. Behind him are a coast with fishing boats, a winding road with travellers, two Roman soldiers (lower right) and olive trees. Paul is large and central rather than small, but there are no blockers and the gold reaches every edge.

Old Adam lies on a woven mat with hands folded on his chest, about ten kin kneel and pray around him, and there are goats, tents, a mud-brick town, a jar and tools; his eyes look slightly open rather than closed. The painting reaches all borders (apart from a tiny dark pixel block in the extreme top-left corner) and there is no lettering.

Unrequested bystanders: a haloed figure gesturing with another man on the left hillside and two old bearded men (one blue-veiled) at right. Faint glyph-like marks sit in the segments of Jesus' cross-nimbus (top center); four kneeling soldiers divide garments and lots in the foreground.

Jesus stands centre in the boat with right arm extended over the water, disciples huddled along both gunwales looking up, torn sail and a lantern hanging from the mast, storm clouds parting to a golden glow. Oil paint reaches all four edges; seen from the side rather than the bow, and a walled town sits on the left shore.

Daniel stands among closed-mouthed lions, with Darius in purple robes leaning over the pit rim. Right of Daniel is a fully formed, glowing winged angel with face, hair and robe. The scene asked only for the faint radiance of an unseen angel.

Job sits upright on a large ash heap strewn with broken jars (centre-right) and gazes up toward a dark whirlwind with fiery glow and storm clouds (upper left-centre); the vortex holds no face, hands or figure. Walled towns sit on both horizons; the painting reaches all four edges and there is no lettering.

Jesus stands center in the boat with right arm extended over the water, disciples around the gunwales look up, lantern on the mast, torn patched sail, clouds parting with pale light. Painting reaches all edges; no lettering.

Several empty wheeled thrones, rendered as wooden chairs engulfed in flame, float in a swirl of cloud and white radiance at upper centre with no figure, face or robe in any seat on close inspection; Daniel in indigo fringed cloak stands at left looking up. Babylon below has small unrequested fires burning among its buildings; dark paint reaches all four edges.

Watercolor: David reclines by a still pool among sheep, with a stone fold and a crook in the grass. The washes fade to white, unpainted paper along the top sky and at the left, right and bottom-left edges.

Jonah sits hunched with his face in his hands, wrapped in a dark cloak, inside a wet, rib-arched cavern; a hazy pale opening at the back (centre-right) shows mist only, with no figure. The view is eye-level with Jonah fairly large rather than small and seen from above; the dark vignette is painted to all edges and there is no lettering.

David's sling pouch (left) still holds a stone after the throw while another stone hovers above Goliath's helmet (right center); Goliath already lies flat on his side rather than falling face-first. Saul and Abner stand in the middle ground right beside the giant instead of watching from the hillside.

Moses (centre-left) raises a hand toward the people with a staff, Aaron beside him, families on both sides, tents around the tabernacle with a smoke column and a cloud-ringed disc of light at top centre (no face), a pig rooting at right-centre and goats and sheep at the corners. Aaron wears a colourful ephod and breastplate of gem settings (no lettering) rather than plain linen; icon gold reaches all edges.

Watercolor: Peter splashes into the shallows clutching his cloak while the beloved disciple points from the boat. Others haul a net of fish, a charcoal fire burns and a faint Jesus stands on the shore. The sky wash stops short, leaving white paper along the top edge and the upper corners.

Abraham raises the knife high (centre) over Isaac, who lies on wood on a stone altar with rope at his wrist, waist and ankles, on a scrubby ridge with a tent at right; the sky holds clouds only. Isaac is a bearded adult rather than small; the painting reaches all edges and there is no lettering.

The cities burn with flames and smoke rising from the rooftops, but no sulfur or fire is shown falling from the sky, so the verse's central action is missing. The distant city at the right horizon has a large dome and minarets (an anachronistic mosque skyline).

Only one six-winged seraph hovers at upper centre, face hidden by a wing but bare feet clearly exposed below the lower wings, and it holds tongs with a burning coal (the later verse 6 moment) rather than veiling its feet as the verse says. Isaiah with a staff at lower left, carved cherubim and palms on the golden walls; radiance contains no figure, and paint reaches all edges.

Jonah sits hunched, head in hands, inside a dark ribbed fish interior. Only a greenish glow appears at the far end, with no figure in it. The right and bottom rims are a slightly lighter grey-green wash, not paper.

A raised gilded icon frame runs around all four borders. The moments are contradictory: a stone is still in David's sling pouch and another is in mid-flight (left-centre) while Goliath already lies face-down with blood and stones by his head (centre-right).

The angel is drawn as a translucent winged woman with folded hands left of Daniel (center-left), though the scene asks only for a faint radiance of an unseen angel. Darius leans over a low wall by a side gate at right instead of over the rim above; lions sleep with closed jaws; God is not depicted.

Abraham at centre-left holds the knife high over Isaac, who lies roped at the waist on split wood atop a stone altar, with a distant tent and a wind-bent tree at right. The watercolour sky shades from blue to a pale cream dawn at upper right but is painted to every edge, and no lettering or signature appears in any corner.

Icon on a gold sky: the father runs with arms flung wide to embrace his bowed son on the village road. Villagers watch from the walls, and terraced hills rise behind. The gold and landscape reach all borders, and there is no lettering.

Yahweh appears only as a dark cloud cut off by the top edge, with fire streaks pouring onto two walled, burning cities; the cloud has no face or figure. Gold-leaf sky and rocky foreground reach all four borders with no lettering in the corners; the tiny fleeing figures at right and the distant town (Zoar) were requested, though no sunrise is visible.

Watercolor washes stop short of the borders: white unpainted paper shows along the lower-left edge, the bottom-right corner and right edge beside the rocks, and the cream sky at top. Paul stands large right of center (not small), face lifted, with the coast, boats, village and travelers on the road behind.

Saul, haloed, walks at centre with face lifted into a cone of white light rays from the top edge (no figure inside the light), with two companions shielding their eyes on each side and walled Damascus at upper right. Icon gold and ground reach all four edges; there are no inscriptions.

Moses holds his staff as the sea parts into a dry path, under a pillar of cloud and fire that contains no figure (top centre). Chariots and wheels already lie sunk among fish in the right-hand sea, the later drowning of the Egyptians, so two moments are mixed.

Wide aerial view of green rolling land under soft cream cumulus filling the upper half; zoomed clouds show no face, hands or figure, so God is shown only as cloud and light. No sea anywhere (the winding channels are dry tan beds), the painting reaches all four edges, and there is no lettering in any corner.

Washes end raggedly before the borders, leaving thin unpainted cream paper slivers along the bottom edge and white gaps at the left and right borders in the sky. Ezekiel stands mid-left with arm raised over a valley of skulls and bones (holding an unrequested blank writing tablet); no figure stands for God.

Plain gold border bands run down the full left and right edges as a painted frame, and a small red signature or initials mark is painted at the bottom-right corner. The scene itself fits: Moses with a staff leads families between teal water walls, and a cloud pillar with flame at top centre (shaped somewhat like a mushroom cloud) holds no face or figure.

Watercolor: the father reaches his bowed son with his hands on the son's shoulders, villagers at the wall. A cursive, signature-like scrawl is hidden in the grass at the bottom-right corner. Unpainted paper shows at the lower left edge and in the pale top band.

Icon-style landscape with a wide dry tan basin where a sea would be, green hills and cypresses, under a gold-leaf sky with swirling pink and blue clouds; neither the clouds nor the mottled gold at the centre form a face or figure, and the painting reaches all four edges. Two tiny light-dotted flecks on the tan path at bottom centre-right (about x 970-1040, y 740) look like grass sprigs at maximum zoom rather than lettering.

Exiles sit on the reedy riverbank with heads bowed and faces in hands; Babylon's walls and ziggurats rise across the water at dusk with lamps glimmering. Painting reaches all four borders; no lettering.

Moses with a staff leads a long column of families carrying children and bundles over wet sand between towering green water walls under a dark night sky. God appears only as a fiery glow inside the clouds at top centre (a weak pillar, no figure), an unrequested walled town sits on the far hill at upper right, and the painting reaches all four edges.
A golden radiance bursts at top centre over dark clouds, dark water and gold rocks, with no figure or face in the light. A uniform dark maroon band about 5px wide runs around all four borders.

A haloed, bearded David in a blue robe reclines in the grass, centre-right, with his hand on a harp, beside a still blue pool, with grazing sheep at left, a stone fold behind and hills under gold leaf; the painting reaches all edges and no lettering appears in the halo, the scabbard or the corners. It departs from the plan: a sheathed sword lies in the grass (bottom centre-right) instead of a shepherd's crook, David is large rather than small in the foreground, and with a halo but no crown his Christ-like face type could be read as Jesus.

The top, left and right borders fade into white paper (vignette). Peter runs left across the water away from Jesus, who glows on the shore at far right; the beloved disciple also points left, and a charcoal fire burns inside the wooden boat instead of on the shore.

Peter clutches his cloak and splashes from the boat (centre) while the young beloved disciple points to a small haloed Jesus on the shore (right); disciples haul a fish-laden net at left. Minor oddity: the charcoal brazier burns inside the wooden boat (centre right) rather than on shore; all four edges painted, no lettering in corners.
A shaft of light breaks through dark clouds at top centre onto wild waves and rocks. The light contains no shape or face, the dark painting continues to all edges, and there is no lettering.

The Shulammite stands at the left third in a red shawl with both hands opened toward roses and lilies, with a shepherd's staff resting at the lower left and vineyards and a stone village behind. The painting reaches all four borders and there is no lettering in any corner.

A gold icon border with an inner bevel runs around all four sides. The Israelites walk across cracked dry seabed between curling water walls, with Moses front-left carrying staffs; the pillar of cloud and fire in the sky (top center) has no face or figure.

Levite stands with knife lowered over the concubine on a mat, lamp at right and the donkey through the grey doorway at left, restrained with no gore. Her eyes are open and gazing upward with a calm face (lower right), so she reads as alive rather than a still body; watercolour reaches all four borders, no lettering.

Watercolor: four soldiers crouch over garments with dice and lots, and the crucified Jesus is in the distance. His titulus carries scribbled glyph marks (top centre-right), and white paper shows on all four borders.

An icon-style painting with a dark red painted border band running down the full left and right edges. The open scroll in the foreground is covered in glyph-like pseudo-script. The soldiers, the woman with a jar and the child in a doorway match the request.

Four Roman soldiers kneel dividing garments, one letting lots fall from his hand, with the crucified figure on a distant cross at upper left (no gore, blank title board) and Jerusalem's walls at right. Pale painted sky reaches the top edge; no lettering.

Only one seraph (centre), a near-nude bronze man whose face and feet are both visible rather than veiled by wings, holding tongs with a burning coal from a later verse; Isaiah (lower left) walks with eyes cast down rather than looking up. The bright cloud behind the seraph holds no figure for God; edges painted to all borders, no lettering.

Watercolor: Moses points with his staff, Aaron is in a breastplate, and a pig roots in the camp among sheep and goats. Above the tabernacle is only a smoke and fire column with no figure. The top sky is bare white paper, and the washes fade to paper at the bottom-right edge.

God appears only as a swirling column of cloud and fire with no figure. A full Egyptian chariot army charges along the far shore at the end of the dry path, and Egyptians are not in the present cast. Unpainted cream paper shows at the right edge and bottom-right corner, where the watercolor wash stops short.

Gold vertical bands with bevel lines run down the left and right sides as a painted frame, and Jesus' cross-nimbus carries letter-like glyphs (center top). The scene itself matches: Jesus calls at the tomb, Lazarus stands wrapped in linens in the doorway, Martha and the crowd watch, and the stone is rolled aside.

David reclines in green grass beside a still pool with grazing sheep and a stone fold (right), hills behind; a harp and sword lie in the grass (lower left) instead of the requested crook, and he is large in the foreground rather than small. Painting reaches all four edges, no lettering.

An open scroll on the wall in the foreground is covered in dense pseudo-Greek lettering. A woman with a jar, Roman soldiers and a child in a doorway complete the street. The scene requested written lines, but legible lettering is still a text defect. Edges are full.

A barefoot child stands near the centre with the wolf and lamb, the leopard and goat, and the calf and lion lying at rest around him. Requested villagers watch from the path at the right, with the walled city and temple on the far hill. The watercolor reaches all edges and there is no lettering.

A haloed child stands at center with wolf and lamb, leopard and goat, calves and a young lion resting around him; villagers watch at right, with the village and distant Jerusalem behind. Gold sky reaches the borders without a frame; no lettering.

Watercolour wash stops short of the borders: bare white paper shows at the top-left corner, along the left edge beside the stone wall, and at the top-right and right edge. Otherwise Paul stands on a hillside path looking up, holding a scroll, with coast, boats, travellers and a red-cloaked soldier below; no lettering.

Watercolor: fire rains from a black cloud onto two walled cities, with smoke, a green plain with palms and small fleeing shapes. There is no face in the clouds. Washes break up at the outer left and right borders, showing cream paper, and white paper shows at the bottom-left corner.

Joshua leads a shouting crowd while priests at the lower right blow shofars and the wall collapses in dust, which matches the request. Two separate golden Arks of the Covenant appear at the upper left: one carried on poles in the middle ground and a second in the haze behind it, duplicating a unique object.

Bald Elisha in a fur-collared mantle walks in the left foreground while youths pour from the Bethel gate pointing and jeering, with villagers in doorways and a golden altar and pole image on the ridge. He walks downhill toward the viewer, away from the city, rather than up toward the gate.

Wide green rolling land under a glowing cream sky with clouds, no sea and no figure or face in the bright centre or clouds. Only tiny paper flecks where the wash breaks at the mid-left and upper-right edges, not a band; no lettering.

Icon style: Daniel stands face lifted among four resting, closed-mouthed lions, with Darius leaning over the rim of a circular stone pit. Beside Daniel is a mandorla-shaped radiance with faint feather lines but no face or body (centre-right). The pit is open-air rather than under a palace; edges are full.

The watercolor vignettes into blank cream paper on all four edges, with the clearest blank areas at the top-left sky, the bottom band and the right edge. Above the tabernacle there are only smoke and radiance lines, with no figure for God. Moses points toward a boar rooting at the right, and Aaron wears an ornate ephod and breastpiece rather than plain linen.
Light breaks from the top center through dark clouds over still dark waters with mist and dim land emerging. There is no face, hand or figure in the light; the painting reaches all edges.

Two near-identical robed royal elders lean over the pit rim (top centre), one crowned and one bareheaded, where only Darius was requested; a visible pale robed human angel figure stands beside Daniel (centre right) though the scene asked for an unseen angel as faint radiance. Daniel and the sleeping lions match; edges full, no lettering.

Moses raises his hand with his staff, Aaron in a breastplate beside him, before a crowd of men, women and children. A smoke and cloud plume rises over the tabernacle with no figure in it. A pig roots among goats at right, and the painting reaches all edges.

Jonah sits hunched and cloaked in a ribbed, dark fish interior over still water, as requested. The scene is cut into an arch with flat gold-leaf spandrels filling the top-left and top-right corners, an icon-style painted frame. The glowing niches in the walls hold only vague light streaks and no clear figure.

Exiles sit on the riverbank at dusk with heads bowed and faces in hands, reeds in the foreground, and Babylon's skyline with lamps across the water. Painting reaches all borders; no lettering in the corners.

Wide green valleys and wildflowers under a luminous cloud-filled sky, horizon open with no sea and no figure or face in the bright sky. Paint reaches all four borders apart from white cloud highlights at the left edge; no lettering.

The father, mid-run with cloak flying and dust rising, clasps his bowed son's head and shoulder. Villagers watch over the wall at left, with a lake and terraced hills beyond. Fully painted edges, no lettering.

Goliath already lies face-down in the centre, yet David's raised sling at the upper left still holds a grey stone in its pouch, so the throw and the fall contradict each other. Saul and Abner watch from the upper right with both armies on the hillsides, and the gold sky reaches all edges.

The sky wash stops short of the top-right corner and right edge, leaving white unpainted paper. Dense pseudo-script lines cover the open scroll on the wall (requested but visible lettering); villagers, soldiers, a woman with a jar and a child in a doorway are present.

Gold-ground icon-style scene: Joshua with sword and spear leads Israelites over the crumbled wall (centre) beside shofar-blowing priests and the ark (right), dust clouds lower left, townsfolk behind the still-standing left wall section. A faint light hairline glyph-like scribble sits in the extreme bottom-right corner, unlike the dark painted grass, reading as a signature mark; gold ground reaches all four edges.

Peter strides on the waves toward Jesus, who stands on the water beneath rays from a dark cloud, while eleven disciples sit in the boat. A painted signature scrawl sits in the waves at the bottom-right corner. The scene is daylit gold rather than night.

The open scroll on the wall at the lower centre is filled with rows of illegible pseudo-script. The scene asks for written lines, so whether this counts as blocking lettering is a policy call. Otherwise the villagers behind the wall, the two Roman soldiers on the road, the woman with a jar and the child in a doorway all match, and the painting reaches all four edges.

Elderly haloed Adam lies on a mat center with eyes closed and hands folded while kin kneel around him, with tents, mudbrick houses, a well and goats behind. Gold sky reaches the edges without a frame; no lettering.

The 'hem of divine glory' is rendered as a literal blue-and-gold embroidered robe train spilling across the floor from both sides (lower half), i.e. clothing standing for God; only one robed seraph (top centre) with its face uncovered, holding tongs and a burning coal from a later verse, though Isaiah does look up. Gold ground and floor reach all borders; facade ornament at top-left is lattice, not lettering.

Golden rays burst from top centre through dark swirling clouds over a dark sea, with a small rocky land emerging at centre. The light contains no figure or face, the dark paint continues to every edge, and there is no lettering.

A bald Elisha in a fur mantle walks with a staff in the left foreground while a band of youths pours from the stone gate at the right, pointing and jeering, and villagers watch from doorways. A golden calf tops the city and a shrine ridge sits at the upper left. He walks away from the gate rather than up toward it, but the moment reads clearly, the watercolor reaches every edge and there is no lettering.

Paul walks a stony hillside path with face lifted, with olive trees, stone walls, the coast with boats, and travelers and soldiers on the road below. He is large and central rather than small, a minor composition deviation; edges are fully painted.

A faint cursive signature is painted into the ground at the bottom-right corner. The wall collapses in dust behind, with priests blowing shofars beside the ark (right), but Joshua and the shouting crowd walk toward the viewer away from the breach rather than into the city.

Watercolor: Jericho's wall collapses in a dust plume. Joshua with a spear points, the crowd shouts with arms raised, and priests blow shofars while carrying the ark. The sky and ground washes stop short of the border, leaving white paper at the top-left, left and bottom edges.

A white-bearded old man in white robes with a radiant head sits on the jeweled throne at the centre, giving God a human form. A small group of people stands in the open doorway at the left. The four creatures wear eye-patterned cloaks rather than bodies full of eyes, and an unrequested golden ark sits before the throne.

The sky wash ends raggedly before the upper-right and upper-left borders, leaving thin strips of white unpainted paper. The scene matches: Saul halts center shading his eyes in a beam of light, companions shield their eyes, and the faint figures in the beam are travelers, not a figure in the light; Damascus is at right.

Watercolour wash stops short of the borders: bare white paper at the top-left and top-right corners and a thin unpainted strip along the left edge. Abraham raises the knife over an adult Isaac bound at the torso on wood atop a stone altar with a tent and sunrise behind; a second sandalled foot dangles oddly at the altar's lower left; no lettering.

Peter leaps from the boat with his cloak as the disciples haul a net and a fire burns on the shore. The figure pointing from the boat (centre-left) is a second haloed, red-robed Christ duplicating the Jesus on the shore (right). The shore Jesus's cross-nimbus also bears small glyph marks.

Jesus stands before the rock tomb with his arm extended toward it, Martha has her hands pressed to her chest beside him, and a crowd frames the foreground. Lazarus is already walking out of the dark entrance at the right in an ordinary white robe and sash, unbound, rather than stirring in grave linens. The edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

The wash fades to white unpainted paper at the bottom-left corner and along the bottom edge, with unpainted cream sky at top-left. Glyph-like lines fill the scroll the elder points to (center); the youth in the doorway, lamp and jar are present.

Jesus's halo (upper centre) has Greek letters 'Ο ΩΝ' painted in the cross arms; otherwise a gold-ground icon of Jesus gesturing toward a linen-wrapped Lazarus standing in the dark tomb mouth, with a haloed woman (Martha) hands to chest at left and crowds on both sides. Painting reaches all four edges, though there is no visible rolled stone and the gold sky is not a late-afternoon light.

Four winged creatures covered in eyes (lion, ox, man, eagle) stand in a glassy sea around an empty radiant throne under a rainbow. The throne holds only light rays, with no figure for God. Domed buildings fill the background, and the gold and sea reach all edges.

The Shulammite stands at left among roses and lilies with a vineyard and stone village to the right. The painting reaches all four edges and no lettering is visible, but the shepherd's staff at lower centre is split in two: the shaft ends bluntly and its crook lies detached in the grass to the right.

Dense columns of pseudo-script cover the open scroll on the wall (center bottom); the scene requests tightly written lines, but this is still visible lettering. Otherwise matches: soldiers walking the road, a woman with a water jar and a child in a doorway at right, villagers at left, with the painting reaching all edges.

Two empty flaming thrones with burning wheels sit in radiant cloud (upper centre-right) with no face, hands or robe in the fire, and Daniel in linen tunic and fringed indigo cloak looks up from a rock above the Babylonian city at left. The only problem is at the edges: in the bottom-right corner (about 25x30 px, running a few px up the right edge) and faintly at the bottom-left, the watercolour wash stops short and cream unpainted paper shows. It is very small, so it is unclear whether it should block release.

David stands after the throw while the stone strikes Goliath's forehead. At upper left, the sling itself, with a stone still in its pouch, flies loose above David's empty hand, a contradictory object state. Goliath falls backward rather than on his face. The cream paper is left blank in the sky and along all borders.

In an icon style, Abraham raises a knife over Isaac, who lies on a plank on a stone altar, with firewood, a tent and wind-bent trees around them. The gold-leaf sky shows no figure and the painting reaches every edge. Isaac is unbound (the rope ties only the plank), the sky is gold rather than dawn, and a second knife lies on the altar as the scene requested.

A white robe and lap rest on the throne seat at center with arms on the armrests, a seated body whose upper part dissolves into light, so God is given form. A red-cloaked white-haired figure stands right of the throne unrequested, and the four creatures (winged man, lion, ox, eagle-headed robed figure) are not covered with eyes.

Moses in a brown cloak and staff stands on the rocky shore (left foreground) with one arm outstretched, while the sea parts into two wave masses around a dry sandy path. God appears only as a glowing orange-white column in the clouds (top centre), with no face or figure in it. Painting is full-bleed with no lettering; the one oddity is wheel ruts on the newly exposed sea bed (centre).

Bald Elisha in a fur mantle walks in the foreground while a band of youths streams from the Bethel gate pointing and jeering, with a golden calf shrine on the ridge (top right). He is walking toward the viewer, away from the gate, rather than up toward it. The painting reaches all edges.

Ezekiel stands at right with his arm raised over a valley of skulls and skeletons, and the sky shows only birds and cloud, with no form for God. At the lower left, and in patches higher up the left border, the watercolour wash stops short and leaves bare white paper at the edge. He also holds an anachronistic clipboard with a metal clip and a pencil (centre-right); its sheet is blank.

The watercolor wash fades to white unpainted paper at the bottom-right corner and lower right edge. David's raised sling (upper left) still holds a stone while another stone flies near Goliath, and Goliath topples sideways onto his hand facing the viewer rather than falling face-first.

Peter (centre-left foreground) strides barefoot across stormy waves toward Jesus, who stands upright on the water at right, while about eight disciples row the small boat behind him (left) under a moonlit break in dark clouds. Painting reaches all four edges with no lettering; small deviations are a pole and fishing net in Peter's hand and a village shoreline close behind the boat.

Watercolor: white-haired Adam lies on a mat with eyes closed and hands clasped on his chest as kin kneel around him. A well, a mudbrick house, tents, goats, a jar and a hoe complete the scene. The washes fade to white paper at the left, bottom and right edges.

Jesus stands at the right end of the boat with an open hand extended, and ten disciples in the boat look up at him. A lantern hangs from the mast, the sail is torn, storm clouds break over rough grey water and a village sits on the right shore. The painting reaches all four edges (the pale patches at the lower corners are water highlights) and there is no lettering. It is lighter than the requested pre-dawn and is seen from the side rather than from the bow.
